By the form of
\mathcal{A}
,
w\not\in[\mathcal{A}]
.
However,
w\not\in[\mathcal{A}^{\mathcal{S}}]
, as follows.
Assume that
w\in[\mathcal{A}^{\mathcal{S}}]
.
By the form of
\mathcal{A}^{\mathcal{S}}
, there are
\mathcal{U}
and
{U}_{0}
such that
\langle{\blacktriangleright},\langle\mathcal{U},{U}_{0}\rangle\rangle\in\delta_{\mathsf{I}}^{\mathcal{A}^{\mathcal{S}}}
,
\langle\langle\mathcal{U},{U}_{0}\rangle,{\blacktriangleleft}\rangle\in\delta_{\mathsf{I}}^{\mathcal{A}^{\mathcal{S}}}
,

\mathtt{A}\in U_{0}
, and
\mathtt{B}\not\in U_{0}
.
By
Lemma

36
,
\mathop{\mathrm{Con}}\nolimits_{\mathcal{A}}^{a}({U}_{0},{U}_{0})\lor\mathop{\mathrm{Con}}\nolimits_{\mathcal{A}}^{\overline{a}}({U}_{0},{U}_{0})
.
In either case,
\mathtt{B}\in U_{0}
, which contradicts
\mathtt{B}\not\in U_{0}
.
Thus
w\not\in[\mathcal{A}^{\mathcal{S}}]
.

VI
Undecidability for
ECoR
*

A
context-free grammar
(CFG)
\mathcal{C}
over a finite set
A
is a tuple
\langle X,\mathcal{R},\mathsf{s}\rangle
, where

•

X
is a finite set of
non-terminal labels
s.t.
A\cap X=\emptyset
;

•

\mathcal{R}
is a finite set of
rewriting rules

x\leftarrow w
of
x\in X
and
w\in(A\cup X)^{*}
;

•

\mathsf{s}\in X
is the
start label
.

The
relation

x\vdash_{\mathcal{C}}w
, where
x\in X
and
w\in A^{*}
, is defined as the minimal relation closed under the following rule:
if
x\leftarrow w_{0}x_{1}w_{1}\dots x_{n}w_{n}\in\mathcal{R}
(where
x,x_{1},\dots,x_{n}\in X
and
w_{0},\dots,w_{n}\in A^{*}
),
then

x_{1}\vdash_{\mathcal{C}}v_{1}
\dots
x_{n}\vdash_{\mathcal{C}}v_{n}
x\vdash_{\mathcal{C}}w_{0}v_{1}w_{1}\dots v_{n}w_{n}

.
The
language

[\mathcal{C}]\subseteq A^{*}
is the set
\{w\mid\mathsf{s}\vdash_{\mathcal{C}}w\}
.
It is well-known that the
universality problem
for CFGs—given a CFG
\mathcal{C}
, does
[\mathcal{C}]=A^{*}
hold?—is
\Pi_{1}^{0}
-complete.

Let
\Gamma
be a set of equations.
We write:

\displaystyle\mathfrak{A}\models\Gamma

\displaystyle\mathrel{\hbox{\hskip 5.0pt\hskip-5.0pt\hbox{$\iff$}\hskip-5.0pt\hskip-2.7431pt\raisebox{4.66875pt}{\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\Delta$}}\hskip-2.7431pt\hskip 5.0pt}}\mathfrak{A}\models t=s\mbox{ for every ${t=s}\in\Gamma$};

\displaystyle\Gamma\models_{\mathrm{REL}}t=s

\displaystyle\mathrel{\hbox{\hskip 5.0pt\hskip-5.0pt\hbox{$\iff$}\hskip-5.0pt\hskip-2.7431pt\raisebox{4.66875pt}{\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\Delta$}}\hskip-2.7431pt\hskip 5.0pt}}\mathfrak{A}\models t=s\mbox{ for every $\mathfrak{A}$ s.t.\ $\mathfrak{A}\models\Gamma$}.

For a CFG
\mathcal{C}=\langle X,\mathcal{R},\mathsf{s}\rangle
and a word
w=a_{1}\dots a_{m}
,
let
\Gamma_{\mathcal{C}}\mathrel{\hbox{\hskip 3.8889pt\hskip-3.8889pt\hbox{$=$}\hskip-3.8889pt\hskip-2.7431pt\raisebox{4.66875pt}{\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\Delta$}}\hskip-2.7431pt\hskip 3.8889pt}}\{w\leq x\mid x\leftarrow w\in\mathcal{R}\}
.
Here,
\ddot{\mathfrak{A}}_{\mathcal{C},w}\mathrel{\hbox{\hskip 3.8889pt\hskip-3.8889pt\hbox{$=$}\hskip-3.8889pt\hskip-2.7431pt\raisebox{4.66875pt}{\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\Delta$}}\hskip-2.7431pt\hskip 3.8889pt}}\mathfrak{A}_{\mathcal{C},w}[0,m]
, where
\mathfrak{A}_{\mathcal{C},w}\mathrel{\hbox{\hskip 3.8889pt\hskip-3.8889pt\hbox{$=$}\hskip-3.8889pt\hskip-2.7431pt\raisebox{4.66875pt}{\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\Delta$}}\hskip-2.7431pt\hskip 3.8889pt}}\langle|\mathfrak{A}|,\{a^{\mathfrak{A}}\}_{a\in A\cup X}\rangle
is the structure over
A\cup X
, defined as follows:

•

|\mathfrak{A}|=[0,m]
;

•

for
a\in A
,
a^{\mathfrak{A}}=\{\langle i-1,i\rangle\mid i\in[1,m]\mbox{ and }a_{i}=a\}
;

•

the elements of
\{x^{\mathfrak{A}}\}_{x\in X}
are the minimal relations closed under the following rule:
if
(w_{0}x_{1}w_{1}\dots x_{n}w_{n}\leq x)\in\Gamma_{\mathcal{C}}
(where
x_{1},\dots,x_{n}\in X
and
w_{0},\dots,w_{n}\in A^{*}
),
then

\hbox{$\vbox{\hbox{\hbox{}\vbox{\hbox{}\vbox{\hbox{\lower 3.21385pt\vbox{\vskip 3.01385pt\hrule height=0.4pt\vskip 3.01385pt\par}}\hbox{\hskip 57.65059pt\hbox{\hbox{\hbox{}\hbox{$\hbox{\hskip 83.57549pt\hskip-83.57549pt\hbox{\hbox{\hskip 83.57549pt\hskip 0.0pt\hbox{}\hskip 0.0pt\hskip-83.57549pt\raisebox{4.0pt}{\hbox{$\langle i_{0},j_{0}\rangle\in\llbracket w_{0}\rrbracket_{\mathfrak{A}}$ \quad$\langle j_{0},i_{1}\rangle\in x_{1}^{\mathfrak{A}}$ \qquad\ldots}}\hskip-83.57549pt\hskip 83.57549pt}}\hskip-83.57549pt\hskip-75.55876pt\raisebox{-12.41226pt}{\hbox{
$\langle j_{n-1},i_{n}\rangle\in x_{n}^{\mathfrak{A}}$ \quad$\langle i_{n},j_{n}\rangle\in\llbracket w_{n}\rrbracket_{\mathfrak{A}}$}}\hskip-75.55876pt\hskip 83.57549pt}$}}\hbox{$\langle i_{0},j_{n}\rangle\in x^{\mathfrak{A}}$}}}\par}\par}}}$}.

For example, if
A=\{(,)\}
,

\mathcal{C}=\langle\{\mathsf{s}\},\{\mathsf{s}\ \leftarrow\ (\mathsf{s})\mathsf{s},\ \mathsf{s}\ \leftarrow\ \mathsf{I}\},\mathsf{s}\rangle
(i.e.,
[\mathcal{C}]
is the Dyck-1 language), and
w=(()())
, then
\mathfrak{A}_{\mathcal{C},w}
is the following:

Then we have the following:

Lemma 47
.

Let
\mathcal{C}=\langle X,\mathcal{R},\mathsf{s}\rangle
be a CFG.
For every
x\in X
and
w\in A^{*}
, the following are equivalent:

1.

x\vdash_{\mathcal{C}}w
;

2.

\ddot{\mathfrak{A}}_{\mathcal{C},w}\models x
;

3.

\Gamma_{\mathcal{C}}\models_{\mathrm{REL}}w\leq x
.

Proof.

1

\Longrightarrow

3
:
By induction on the derivation tree of
x\vdash_{\mathcal{C}}w
.
This derivation tree is of the following form:

x_{1}\vdash_{\mathcal{C}}v_{1}
\dots
x_{n}\vdash_{\mathcal{C}}v_{n}
x\vdash_{\mathcal{C}}w_{0}v_{1}w_{1}\dots v_{n}w_{n}

,
where
n\in\mathbb{N}
,
x_{1},\dots,x_{n}\in X
,
w_{0},\dots,w_{n}\in A^{*}
,
v_{1},\dots,v_{n}\in A^{*}
s.t.
w=w_{0}v_{1}w_{1}\dots v_{n}w_{n}
and
x\leftarrow w_{0}x_{1}w_{1}\dots x_{n}w_{n}\in\mathcal{R}
.
W.r.t.
\Gamma_{\mathcal{C}}\models_{\mathrm{REL}}
, we have

\displaystyle w

\displaystyle=w_{0}v_{1}w_{1}\dots v_{n}w_{n}

\displaystyle\leq w_{0}x_{1}w_{1}\dots x_{n}w_{n}

(
\Gamma_{\mathcal{C}}\models_{\mathrm{REL}}v_{i}\leq x_{i}
for
i\in[n]
(IH))

\displaystyle\leq x.

(
(w_{0}x_{1}w_{1}\dots x_{n}w_{n}\leq x)\in\Gamma_{\mathcal{C}}
)

Hence
\Gamma_{\mathcal{C}}\models_{\mathrm{REL}}w\leq x
.

3

\Longrightarrow

2
:
Because
\mathfrak{A}_{\mathcal{C},w}\models\Gamma_{\mathcal{C}}
and
\ddot{\mathfrak{A}}_{\mathcal{C},w}\models w
hold.

2

\Longrightarrow

1
:
We show the following:

Sublemma
.

For every
i,j\in[0,m]
and
x\in X
,
if
\mathfrak{A}_{\mathcal{C},w}[i,j]\models x
, then
i\leq j
and
x\vdash_{\mathcal{C}}a_{i}\dots a_{j-1}
.

Proof.

By induction on the derivation tree from the definition of
\{x^{\mathfrak{A}_{\mathcal{C},w}}\}_{x\in X}
.
This derivation tree is of the following form

\langle i_{0},j_{0}\rangle\in\llbracket w_{0}\rrbracket_{\mathfrak{A}_{\mathcal{C},w}}

\langle j_{0},i_{1}\rangle\in x_{1}^{\mathfrak{A}_{\mathcal{C},w}}
…

\langle j_{n-1},i_{n}\rangle\in x_{n}^{\mathfrak{A}_{\mathcal{C},w}}

\langle i_{n},j_{n}\rangle\in\llbracket w_{n}\rrbracket_{\mathfrak{A}_{\mathcal{C},w}}

\langle i_{0},j_{n}\rangle\in x^{\mathfrak{A}_{\mathcal{C},w}}

,
where
x_{1},\dots,x_{n}\in X
,
w_{0},\dots,w_{n}\in A^{*}
,

i_{0},j_{0},\dots,i_{n},j_{n}\in|\mathfrak{A}_{\mathcal{C},w}|
,
and
\langle i_{0},j_{n}\rangle=\langle i,j\rangle
.
By the definition of
a^{\mathfrak{A}_{\mathcal{C},w}}
(where
a\in A
), we have
i_{k}\leq j_{k}
and
w_{k}=a_{i_{k}}\dots a_{j_{k}-1}
.
By IH, we have
j_{k-1}\leq i_{k}
and
x_{k}\vdash_{\mathcal{C}}a_{j_{k-1}}\dots a_{i_{k}-1}
.
Combining them yields
i\leq j
and
x\vdash_{\mathcal{C}}a_{i}\dots a_{j-1}
(because
x\leftarrow w_{0}x_{1}w_{1}\dots x_{n}w_{n}\in\mathcal{R}
).
∎

By specializing this sub-lemma with
\langle i,j\rangle=\langle 0,m\rangle
, this completes the proof.
∎

Lemma 48
.

For every CFG
\mathcal{C}=\langle X,\mathcal{R},\mathsf{s}\rangle
, we have

[\mathcal{C}]=A^{*}\quad\iff\quad\Gamma_{\mathcal{C}}\models_{\mathrm{REL}}A^{*}\leq\mathsf{s}.

(Here,
A^{*}
denotes the term
(a_{1}\cup\dots\cup a_{n})^{*}
in the right-hand side, where
A=\{a_{1},\dots,a_{n}\}
.)

Proof.

We have

\displaystyle[\mathcal{C}]=A^{*}

\displaystyle\iff\forall w\in A^{*}.\ \mathsf{s}\vdash_{\mathcal{C}}w

(Def. of
[]
)

\displaystyle\iff\forall w\in A^{*}.\ \Gamma_{\mathcal{C}}\models_{\mathrm{REL}}w\leq\mathsf{s}

(
Lemma

47
)

\displaystyle\iff\Gamma_{\mathcal{C}}\models_{\mathrm{REL}}A^{*}\leq\mathsf{s}.

∎

Additionally, we prepare the following deduction lemma for
Hoare hypotheses

{u}=\bot
(cf.
[
34
, Thm. 4.1]
for KAT):

Lemma 49
.

For every
{\textrm{ECoR}}*
terms
t,s,{u}
and every set
\Gamma
of equations,
we have

\Gamma\cup\{{u}=\bot\}\models_{\mathrm{REL}}t\leq s\iff\Gamma\models_{\mathrm{REL}}t\leq s\cup(\top{u}\top).

Proof.

We have

\displaystyle\Gamma\cup\{{u}=\bot\}\models_{\mathrm{REL}}t\leq s

\displaystyle\iff\mbox{for every ${\mathfrak{A}}[x,y]$ s.t.\ $\mathfrak{A}\models\Gamma\cup\{{u}=\bot\}$,}

{\mathfrak{A}}[x,y]\models t\leq s

(Def. of
\models_{\mathrm{REL}}
)

\displaystyle\iff\mbox{for every ${\mathfrak{A}}[x,y]$ s.t.\ $\mathfrak{A}\models\Gamma$ and ${\mathfrak{A}}[x,y]\not\models\top{u}\top$,}

{\mathfrak{A}}[x,y]\models t\leq s

(
\clubsuit
1)

\displaystyle\iff\mbox{for every ${\mathfrak{A}}[x,y]$ s.t.\ $\mathfrak{A}\models\Gamma$,}

\displaystyle\hskip 100.00015pt{\mathfrak{A}}[x,y]\models t\leq s\cup(\top{u}\top)

(
\clubsuit
2)

\displaystyle\iff\Gamma\models_{\mathrm{REL}}t\leq s\cup(\top{u}\top).

(Def. of
\models_{\mathrm{REL}}
)

Here, (

♣

1
) is because
\mathfrak{A}\models{u}=\bot\iff\llbracket{u}\rrbracket_{\mathfrak{A}}=\emptyset\iff{\mathfrak{A}}[x,y]\not\models\top{u}\top
.
(
VI
) is because:

\displaystyle({\mathfrak{A}}[x,y]\not\models\top{u}\top)\mbox{ implies }({\mathfrak{A}}[x,y]\models t\leq s)

\displaystyle\iff{\mathfrak{A}}[x,y]\models\top{u}\top\ \lor\ {\mathfrak{A}}[x,y]\not\models t\ \lor\ {\mathfrak{A}}[x,y]\models s

\displaystyle\iff{\mathfrak{A}}[x,y]\not\models t\ \lor\ {\mathfrak{A}}[x,y]\models s\cup(\top{u}\top)

\displaystyle\iff{\mathfrak{A}}[x,y]\models t\leq s\cup(\top{u}\top).

∎

By
Lemmas

48
,
49
, we have the following:

Theorem 50
.

The equational theory of
{\textrm{ECoR}}*
is
\Pi_{1}^{0}
-complete.

Proof.

For upper bound:
By
Lemma

22
.
For hardness:
Let
\mathcal{C}=\langle X,\{x_{i}\leftarrow w_{i}\mid i\in[n]\},\mathsf{s}\rangle
be a CFG.
Then we have

\displaystyle[\mathcal{C}]=A^{*}

\displaystyle\iff\{w_{i}\leq x_{i}\mid i\in[n]\}\models_{\mathrm{REL}}A^{*}\leq\mathsf{s}

(
Lemma

48
)

\displaystyle\iff\{w_{i}\cap x_{i}^{-}=\bot\mid i\in[n]\}\models_{\mathrm{REL}}A^{*}\leq\mathsf{s}

(For every
\mathfrak{A}
,
\mathfrak{A}\models w_{i}\leq x_{i}\iff\mathfrak{A}\models w_{i}\cap x_{i}^{-}=\bot
)

\displaystyle\iff{}\models_{\mathrm{REL}}A^{*}\leq\mathsf{s}\cup\left(\bigcup_{i=1}^{n}\top(w_{i}\cap x_{i}^{-})\top\right)

(
Lemma

49
)

\displaystyle\iff{}\models_{\mathrm{REL}}A^{*}\leq\mathsf{s}\cup\left(\bigcup_{i=1}^{n}(a\cup a^{-})(w_{i}\cap x_{i}^{-})(a\cup a^{-})\right).

(
{}\models_{\mathrm{REL}}\top=a\cup a^{-}
, where
a
is some element in
A
.)

Thus we can reduce the universality problem for CFGs, which is
\Pi_{1}^{0}
-hard, to the equational theory of
{\textrm{ECoR}}*
(precisely,
\mathcal{T}_{\{\cdot,\cup,\cap,\_^{*}\}}
with the complement of term variables).
∎

VII
Conclusion and future work

We have studied the computational complexity of existential calculi of relations with transitive closure, using edge saturations.
A natural interest is to extend our complexity results for more general syntaxes.
We believe that the upper bound results for intersection-free fragments hold even if we extend them with
tests
in KAT (by considering
guarded strings

[
35
]
instead of words (strings), in saturable paths); e.g.,
KAT with top
(w.r.t. binary relations), which are recently studied for modeling
incorrectness logic

[
36
,
37
,
24
,
25
]
.

Another future work is to study the axiomatizability of them.
Unfortunately, the equational theory of (full)
{\textrm{ECoR}}*
is not finitely axiomatizable because it is not recursively enumerable (
Theorem

50
);
but we leave it open to finding some complete (finite) axiomatization for its fragments, including KA terms with complements of term variables.
(The equation (
1
) indicates that, at least, we need axioms of KA with top w.r.t. binary relations
[
24
]
.)
